A1.justification: Despite the changed title and organization, both PDFs describe SQUK and SRC. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, calibration and backbone comparisons, soft-requirement ablations, and an evaluation against LLMs.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional LLM comparison results in Table 4.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 adds a sparsity-based inference optimization using thresholded matrix storage and selected state-vector rows for leaf elimination. The node-elimination framework, debiasing, affine calibration, and training objective remain unchanged; the newly explicit calibration parameterization documents the existing component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CN15k, PPI5k, O*NET20k, twelve soft-query types, and the CN15k natural-language multiple-choice task. Although v2's Section 5.1 omits 2U and UP from its list, both remain in its results and query-structure figure.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds Llama3.3 70B and Gemini-1.5-pro alongside the retained GPT models. The main benchmark comparator set remains unchanged. FIT is newly identified as the source of SRC's forward inference, without becoming a separate additional comparison row.

E3.justification: The reported query counts, soft-requirement settings, ranking metrics, and hyperparameter searches are retained. The LLM evaluation still uses 370 manually checked queries, four candidates per query, and the same substantive prompt; adding models does not revise this protocol.

E4.justification: New Appendix C adds an LLM error case involving weighted bread/rice constraints. The soft-requirement ablation moves from v1 Section 6.2 to v2 Appendix B, while the existing backbone analysis is retained. These relocations do not constitute new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report performance point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or experimental error bars. No empirical uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds accuracies of 42.6 for Llama3.3 70B and 37.1 for Gemini-1.5-pro; GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4-preview, and SRC retain 34.3, 37.8, and 48.9. Existing benchmark and ablation scores are unchanged. v2 also reports 3.4% matrix sparsity and 97% storage reduction, while removing v1's graph-summary statistics.

T1.justification: v2 adds sparsity-dependent complexity reasoning and explicitly states monotonicity and below-one properties for the error-bound function. The inference lemmas and two error theorems retain their substantive proofs, moved from Appendices D/J to H/N.

C1.justification: v2 shifts the central framing from open-world reasoning to incomplete knowledge graphs and emphasizes calibration's advantage over generalized symbolic methods as well as query embeddings. The principal SQUK, SRC, complexity, and error-control contributions remain.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly explains that the evaluation does not fully realize the open-world assumption, and Section 8 explicitly discusses scope limitations and missing cyclic-query experiments. v2 also adds arithmetic and hallucination interpretations of LLM failures, while retaining the existing calibration interpretations.

D1.justification: v2 supplies explicit affine-calibration parameter formulas and identifies Nvidia V100-32G hardware. Conversely, v1 Table 7's entity, relation, fact-count, and confidence-distribution statistics disappear, leaving an unresolved table reference in Appendix K. These are documentation changes, not evidence of changed datasets.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the CWA/OWA distinction and applications, including Reiter, Yang et al. (2022b), and Bai et al. (2024a,b), while removing several earlier citations. It more explicitly positions SRC's forward inference as generalized from FIT; the main related-work survey remains largely intact.

P1.justification: The title, introduction, definitions, terminology, and explanatory narrative are extensively rewritten. Logical-query preliminaries move into Appendix D, the soft-requirement discussion moves into Appendix B, and the appendices are substantially reorganized. Author and affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and extensively rearranges displays. It adds a simplified SRC illustration while retaining the earlier diagram, moves the query-structure figure and ablation table into appendices, repeats training counts in the main text, expands the LLM table, and removes the graph-statistics table.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful calibration details, hardware information, LLM comparisons, and a clearer qualification of its open-world claims. However, it removes graph statistics, leaves unresolved references, and introduces an inconsistent case study: Appendix C names bread and rice as answers although neither is among its candidates. With the central results and proofs retained, these benefits and documentation regressions leave the net quality direction uncertain.
